clips.text: the modern suspicion of beauty was really, really cemented in 1908 by Adolf Luce's infamous essay, Ornament and Crime, which basically declared that all architectural and artistic decoration was immoral and against progress. He wrote, the evolution of culture is synonymous with the removal of ornament from utilitarian objects. This is basically the idea of form follows function and it's exactly why everything from street lamps to doorknobs to park benches went from beautiful and well-designed with artistic flourish to sterile and ugly. The philosophy of modernism turned beauty into something shameful and something to be eliminated in the name of honesty, efficiency, and purity.
